newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen down on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen down on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares eased to 16,968.8 points after a four-session gain and analysts said the stronger selling after price-fixing and at continuous trade signalled another fall on Friday as the market levelled out.

"Most stocks seem fairly valued or slightly expensive but there's not a big potential for falls," said Roman Sosnowski of Bank Staropolski brokerage, who said the bourse could stay in a channel between 16,000 and 17,000 points.
Analysts said recent optimistic inflation forecasts and good March earnings by several firms could keep the market mood good.
The main market's all share WIG index eased 0.3 percent to 16,968.8 ponts and turnover fell 22.3 percent to 194.2 million zlotys on all three markets.
Analysts said the recent strong performance by construction firms ahead of the summer season could continue and help buoy the overall market.
Remak, up 5.5 percent, led builders on Thursday, also seen benefiting from last week's news it saw its 1997 net profit rising to 987,000 zlotys from 100,000 zlotys last year.
Analysts said the current busy primary market schedule could dampen buying in coming sessions.
The state treasury sale of 2,976,560 shares in metals trader and producer Impexmetal shares at a mininimum price of 36 zlotys lasts until April 30.
Analysts said Espebepe tumbled 9.5 percent as it returned to large speculative swings based on whether the ailing builder would receive a debt restructuring deal.

Paper firm Celuloza Swiecie, which starts main market trade on Friday, could open as high as 25 zlotys after selling at 20.5 zlotys at a special bourse session earlier this week, though its upside could prove limited due to weak first quarter earnings, analysts said.
